values: Cynthia’s Homeschool Music Journey — Sample Program
Ages 6–12 • 3 mastery levels • 108 lessons • piano, strings & percussion • solo, parent-child & family modes
Program design
Three 36-lesson levels; each contains six units with a repeatable six-lesson arc.
Level
Learner Promise
Mastery Demonstration
Lessons
Suggested Pace
Recommended pace
1–2 lessons weekly. Repeat, split, or extend a lesson when mastery needs more time.
Level 1 — Discover
I can keep a steady beat, recognize musical patterns, and play short pieces with healthy habits.
Perform an 8–16 beat piece on a chosen instrument, keep a part with others, and explain one musical choice.
18–36 weeks
Lesson length
Level 1: 30–40 min • Level 2: 40–50 min • Level 3: 45–60 min
Level 2 — Build
I can read and create simple musical ideas, coordinate both hands or multiple techniques, and rehearse with a partner.
Perform a 16–32 measure or equivalent piece with steady pulse, accurate patterns, expressive contrast, and recovery after a mistake.
18–36 weeks
Instrument path
Every lesson offers piano, string, and percussion routes. Families may specialize or rotate.
Level 3 — Create & Lead
I can interpret, arrange, improvise, compose, and lead music using evidence from what I hear and see.
Plan and lead a polished 3–5 minute capstone containing performance, arrangement or composition, improvisation, and spoken reflection.
24–36 weeks
Mastery rule
Advance when the learner demonstrates the level outcome—not merely when all lessons are viewed.
Cynthia’s method
The ‘Method Lens’ field is intentionally editable so Cynthia can replace sample language with her signature teaching approach.
Developmental Design for Ages 6–12
Safety note
Adults supervise instrument setup; protect hearing; use age-appropriate instruments and safe movement.
Ages 6–7
Imitation before explanation
Icons, movement, two- to four-beat chunks
Adult support recommended
Celebrate short successful repetitions
Ages 8–9
Connect sound to symbol
Four- to eight-beat patterns and choices
Coach prompts, then independence
Name one strength and next step
Ages 10–12
Explain, revise, and lead
Notation, arranging, research, and projects
Peer/mentor relationship
Use evidence in reflection
Mixed ages
One concept, tiered parts
Easy pulse + medium pattern + challenge lead
Rotate roles
Assess each learner against own part
